items.title: Shirudo: OpenAI and Cisco's open-source runtime for shielding unpatched Linux
items.summary: Shirudo is an open-source runtime by OpenAI and Cisco that uses eBPF to deploy temporary security shields on running Linux systems without requiring restarts. It allows operators to block specific vulnerable code paths, such as the Java4Shell exploit, while legitimate requests continue to process.
items.why_it_matters: It addresses the operational gap where patching takes days or weeks, enabling teams to maintain service availability by blocking exploits without taking systems offline.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `docker run openai/shirudo:latest` on a test service.

items.title: Why millions of agents don't need millions of VMs on Agent Substrate
items.summary: Agent Substrate 1.0 is an open-source Kubernetes runtime that separates agent workspaces from machines, allowing a single worker to host up to 1,000 actors in isolated sandboxes. It suspends idle agents by saving memory and files to disk or Cloud Storage, then wakes them in under a second on any available worker.
items.why_it_matters: It resolves the inefficiency of dedicated VMs or Pods where resources remain reserved during idle waits, enabling efficient scaling to millions of agents by freeing compute resources while preserving state.
items.next_step_detail: Spin up a small Agent Substrate instance following the quick‑start guide and benchmark agent launch latency.

items.title: Your agent's tool registry is an API. Stop reviewing it like config.
items.summary: An agent's tool registry functions as an API surface where tools carry authority, requiring explicit declaration of action type, identity, data scope, and approval requirements to prevent unreviewed privilege escalation. Practical controls include making authority changes visible in diffs, enforcing runtime checks, and treating tool additions with the same rigor as public endpoint reviews.
items.why_it_matters: Treating the registry as an API surface ensures that authority changes, such as scope expansion or approval removal, are visible in code reviews and enforced at runtime, preventing the accumulation of over-privileged credentials that bypass model-level controls.
items.next_step_detail: Read and apply the API‑centric checklist to your current agent tool registry.
